steps.title: Welcome to Pipelinq
steps.body: A few quick choices to get your CRM, pipeline and service desk ready. Only the reporting currency is required — everything else is optional and can be changed later in the admin settings.

steps.title: Reporting currency
steps.body: Used to format revenue, forecast and pipeline amounts across dashboards and reports.

steps.title: Provision data
steps.body: Create the Pipelinq OpenRegister register and schemas, plus the default sales pipeline and stages, service queues, agent skills, lead sources and request channels. This normally runs automatically on install; run it here if OpenRegister was enabled after Pipelinq, or to repair a partial install. It is safe to run more than once.

steps.title: Demo data (optional)
steps.body: Seed a small linked demo dataset — clients, leads, requests and contactmomenten — so lists, dashboards and the 360° client view show a working product right away. Optional and safe to run more than once; every object is marked [Demo] and can be removed later with `occ pipelinq:demo:seed --remove`. Skip this on a production install.

steps.title: Organisation
steps.body: Your organisation details, printed on POS receipts and shown on reports. Optional — leave blank to skip.

steps.title: Integrations
steps.body: Optional connections to other Conduction apps. Set the Shillinq base URL to surface recurring-revenue metrics and route billing/ledger entries; set the XWiki URL to embed the knowledge base. Leave blank to disable.

steps.title: All set
steps.body: Pipelinq is ready. Head to the Dashboard or Leads to get started.

steps.title: Welcome to Pipelinq
steps.body: Let's walk the core sales journey together — from a product to a billed contract. You'll create each record yourself, in your own workspace.
First, your catalogue. Open Products from the menu.
Add the product or service you sell — we'll put it on the quotation later.
steps.task: Click New and save a product

steps.body: Add the person or organisation you're selling to.
steps.task: Click New and save a contact

steps.body: A lead is a sales opportunity. Open Leads.
Create a lead for this opportunity and link the contact you just made.
steps.task: Click New and save a lead

steps.body: The pipeline shows every lead by stage. Drag your lead forward as it progresses.
steps.task: Open the Pipeline and move your lead to the next stage

steps.body: Quote the lead. In Pipelinq a signable quotation IS the contract — one record, no duplication.
steps.task: Open Contracts and create a quotation

steps.title: Your quote is the contract
steps.body: Once the customer signs the quotation it becomes the contract automatically — the same record carries the agreed lines, price and signature.

steps.title: Send it for billing
steps.body: Finally, hand the signed contract to Shillinq for invoicing and ledger posting — that closes the loop from product to paid.
steps.task: Continue in Shillinq to invoice this contract

pages._note: The Customer Satisfaction KPI (SatisfactionKpiWidget, widget id 'satisfaction', layout slot 17) was removed 2026-07 because its data source is permanently empty (AnalyticsService hardcodes no survey responses after the forms-leaf migration); it returns with real CSAT data via openspec change customer-satisfaction-closed-loop.

Client 360 record as a declarative type:detail page (pipelinq-client-contact-detail-declarative). Identity + account/relationship fields auto-render in the body (CnObjectDataWidget; name/email/phone/address/website are sourced from the linked NC contact and stay read-only via the index fieldOverrides). KPI chips come from summaryAggregates; related lists (contacts/leads/requests/projecten/contactmomenten/complaints, FK 'client') from relatedCollections; the rich sub-features (Relationships / Activity / Communication / Bookings / contactmoment quick-log) stay in the page body via bodyWidgets registered as kind:'section'. KEPT-AS-NOTE: (1) the 'Edit in Contacts' deep-link and the delete-with-linked-entity warning have no declarative primitive — the page Delete uses CnDetailPage's standard delete and 'Edit in Contacts' is reachable from the linked NC contact; (2) summaryAggregates filters are equality-only, so 'Open leads'=status:open (the lead enum is open|won|lost) and 'Open requests' counts status:new (in_progress not expressible as one equality chip); (3) the contactmoment quick-log no longer auto-refreshes the related list on save — use the page Refresh action.
pages.title: Client

config._note: Customer-360 archetype. A client is the account hub of the CRM: everything (contacts, deals, requests, contracts, projects, complaints, interactions) hangs off it via FK 'client' (contract via 'clientRef'). ADR-062 rev3: the lead row is a field-split data pair — Identity (name/email/phone/address/website, the read-only NC-contact mirror) 8-wide + a stats-block KPI card top-right (open/won pipeline count & value, new requests, @objectId-scoped) — with the Account data widget (type/industry/notes) and the comms Email/Files leaves below; child relationships stay FK-scoped related-collection tables plus the Relationships/Activity/Bookings/Messages/quick-log app sections. Contracts are a first-class collection because recurring revenue is core to a customer view. summaryAggregates chips retired to the in-grid stats-block (rule 2). Sidebar is audit-only.

Service-request case archetype. A handler works a request to resolution, so the body leads with the request fields + related graph (client, contact, pipeline, queue), then the comms-centric Email and Files leaves (a request is inherently correspondence-driven). Below, two FK-scoped child tables surface the work generated by the request: the contactmomenten logged against it (FK 'request') and the follow-up tasks (FK 'requestId'); an in-grid stats-block (rule 2, replacing the retired summaryAggregates chips) counts open tasks and logged contactmomenten @objectId-scoped. lifecycleActions drives the OR-authoritative status transitions (new -> in_progress -> completed/rejected/converted). The RequestConversionSection app widget stays in the body for the case-to-Procest conversion. Generic Deck/Flow/Time/Knowledge/Forms leaves dropped from the sidebar per the audit-only rule.

Case archetype (bespoke-detail-pages). A complaint is a service case a case-handler works to resolution against an SLA, so the body leads with the case fields (status / priority / channel / SLA deadline + slaStatus / assignedTo) at 8-wide and the related graph (client, contact, task) at 4-wide, then Documents (evidence, correspondence attachments) full-width. Comms leaves are NOT on the body: the complaint schema declares no email/calendar/talk linkedType, so per the hard rule they stay off — a complaint communicates via its linked client/contact records. lifecycleActions drives the OR-authoritative status transitions (new -> in_progress -> resolved/rejected). Generic Deck/Flow/Timeline leaves were dropped from the sidebar per the audit-only rule; the immutable change history is the only sidebar tab.

pages._note: Contact record as a declarative type:detail page (pipelinq-client-contact-detail-declarative). The contact-person fields (role, email, phone, client FK) auto-render in the body (CnObjectDataWidget; name/email/phone are read-only NC-contact mirror via the index fieldOverrides). The parent-organisation link is a relationLinks entry (fkField 'client', labelField 'name') — its search-and-link modal replaces the bespoke CnFormDialog organisation linker, and the linked client is shown by the auto data widget's 'client' field. BRP / Relationships / Communication stay in the page body via bodyWidgets registered as kind:'section'. KEPT-AS-NOTE: (1) the bespoke 'Parent Organisation' card also rendered the client name+type as a clickable deep-link; the declarative client FK shows the id/name in the data widget and relationLinks drives the link/relink — the separate type-line is dropped; (2) BrpContactPanel emits @contact-updated to trigger a re-fetch — in declarative mode the panel updates the contact server-side and the user refreshes via the page Refresh action; (3) 'Edit in Contacts' deep-link has no declarative primitive — identity is editable from the linked NC contact.
pages.title: Contact

config._note: Person archetype (contact-360). A salesperson opening a contact sees the person's details, their comms leaves (Email + Meetings calendar — a contact is a real correspondent with vCard email/phone) and files on the main body. Below, FK-scoped child tables surface everything this person drives: their deals (lead.contact), their requests (request.contact) and their appointments (booking.customerId); an in-grid stats-block (rule 2, replacing the retired summaryAggregates chips) counts open-deal count/value @objectId-scoped. BRP/BSN compliance + relationship graph stay as end-of-page app sections; the parent-organisation link stays a relationLink. Sidebar is audit-only.

pages._note: LeadList.vue extends a CnIndexPage with lead-specific bulk controls (NcCheckboxRadioSwitch quick-filters plus CnMassImportDialog / CnMassExportDialog) that the declarative 'index' page type does not expose; kept as a host-app component until those bulk actions are promoted to the library.
pages.title: Leads

config._note: Opportunity/deal archetype. The main body surfaces what a salesperson looks at every visit — the deal fields (value, probability, stage, expected close), the related graph (client, contact, pipeline) and the comms leaves (Email / Files / Meetings — a deal is actively worked over correspondence). ADR-062 rev3: the data widget is field-split into Deal (title/value/probability/expectedClose/priority/status) and Qualification (source/stage/stageOrder/qualificationScore/assignee/description/notes); a stats-block KPI card top-right (rule 2, replacing the retired summaryAggregates) shows deal value + line count @objectId-scoped. A full-width object-list of the deal's line items (leadProduct, FK 'lead', allowCreate ON so a line pre-links the deal) shows what is being quoted. lifecycleActions drives the OR-authoritative pipeline status (open -> won/lost). Generic Deck/Flow/Time/Knowledge/Forms leaves dropped from the sidebar per the audit-only rule.

content.emptyText: No products quoted on this deal yet — add a line to build the quote.

config._note: Interaction-log archetype (bespoke-detail-pages). A contactmoment is the immutable record of a single interaction (call / email / chat / CTI-telephony), so it reads like a log entry, not a workspace: the interaction fields (channel, subject, outcome/disposition, agent, direction, timestamps, duration, CTI extension) fill the body 8-wide, with the related parties (client, contact, request) at 4-wide for one-click drill-through. Documents full-width carries the call recording (recording_url) and any attached correspondence. NO email/calendar body widgets — contactmoment declares no comms linkedType and is itself the communication record, not a live mailbox. There are no child collections, so no object-list; a lean two-row grid keeps it fast to scan.

Task/action-item archetype (bespoke-detail-pages). A task is a to-do an agent works to completion, so the body leads with the execution fields (type, status, priority, deadline, assignee user/group, callbackPhoneNumber, preferredTimeSlot, attempts, resultText) 8-wide and the source records it hangs off (client, request, originating contactmoment) at 4-wide. Documents full-width for any attached result artefact. NO email/calendar body widgets — task declares no comms linkedType; a callback task carries the phone number as a field, not a live mailbox. No child collection, so no object-list.

pages._note: ProductBarcodeSearch.vue is a single-purpose scanner surface: a barcode/EAN input that resolves one product and shows an NcEmptyContent fallback when nothing matches; it is neither a list nor an object-detail page, so no standard page type fits.
pages.title: Barcode lookup

config._note: Catalog archetype (bespoke-detail-pages). A product is a catalog master, not a conversation — so there are deliberately NO comms leaves (product declares no email/calendar linkedType). The body leads with the catalog fields (name, sku/barcode/gtin, unitPrice/cost/taxRate/btwClass, category, type, unit, variants/modifierGroups/priceTiers) 8-wide and the related graph (category, preferredSupplier, MDM masterEntityRef) at 4-wide. A stats-block KPI card (rule 2, replacing the retired summaryAggregates) chips the live On-deals count @objectId-scoped; below sits a read-only object-list of the deal lines that reference this product (leadProduct, FK 'product', allowCreate:false — deal lines are authored on the deal, never from the catalog) so a product manager can see demand at a glance, then the product image/spec files full-width. Two-tone grid (catalog + usage) makes it read very differently from the comms-first person pages.

content.emptyText: This product is not on any deal lines yet.

pages._note: POS refund record as a declarative type:detail page (pipelinq-pos-mdm-detail-declarative). The refund's flat fields (reference / originalTransaction / cashier / status / refundReason / paymentMethod / refundAmount / totalTax / confirmedAt / rejectedAt / notes / …) auto-render in the body via CnObjectDataWidget. The parts no declarative primitive can express live in one kind:'section' bodyWidget (PosRefundActionsSection, after-data): the manager-gated Bevestigen / Afwijzen actions and the 'Returned items' table. KEPT-AS-NOTE: (1) lifecycleActions is NOT wired — the actions POST to bespoke /api/pos-refunds/{id}/{action} endpoints (NOT OR /transition) and posRefund has no x-openregister-lifecycle; (2) the 'Returned items' table stays in the section because it is a CROSS-SCHEMA JOIN — each posRefundLine row is enriched with its original posTransactionLine (description + original quantity, via the line's originalLine pointer) and relatedCollections renders ONE schema and cannot resolve a column off a second schema. Missing primitives: a relatedCollections column resolved off a SECOND schema (cross-schema join lookup); the host-app-endpoint action toolbar (see PosTransactionDetail).
pages.title: Retour

config._note: FINANCIAL archetype (bespoke-detail-pages). A POS refund is a credit-side ledger record, so NO comms leaves (posRefund declares no email/calendar linkedType). The body opens with two KPI stat cards (Refund amount / Tax) then the refund fields (reference, originalTransaction, cashier, status, refundReason, paymentMethod/reference, confirmed/rejected timestamps) 8-wide and the related graph (original transaction, cashier) 4-wide. The returned lines render as an object-list (posRefundLine, FK 'refund') giving the plain per-line quantities/totals; the manager-gated Bevestigen/Afwijzen actions and the CROSS-SCHEMA-JOIN 'Returned items' table (each line enriched from its original posTransactionLine) stay in the PRESERVED PosRefundActionsSection bodyWidget — that join cannot be expressed by a single-schema object-list, exactly as the section's note records. Audit-trail moves to a sidebar tab.

content.emptyText: No returned lines — refund lines are computed from the original transaction, not added by hand.

pages._note: CashShiftList.vue is a CnIndexPage specialised for the cash-drawer shift register (shift-specific columns/state on the cashShift schema); kept as a host-app component while those presets live outside the library.
pages.title: Kassalade

pages._note: Cash-shift record as a declarative type:detail page (pipelinq-pos-mdm-detail-declarative). The shift's flat float fields (reference / drawer / operator / managedBy / currency / floatAmount / floatAt / status / closedAt / reconciliationStatus / notes) auto-render in the body via CnObjectDataWidget; the drops render as a relatedCollections table (cashDrop, FK 'shift'). The parts no declarative primitive can express live in one kind:'section' bodyWidget (CashShiftActionsSection, after-related): the cash-reconciliation VARIANCE panel and the drop/count/reconcile actions. KEPT-AS-NOTE: (1) lifecycleActions is NOT wired — Geld verwijderen (drop) / Shift afsluiten en tellen (count) / reconcile POST to bespoke /api/pos-shifts/{id}/{drop|count|diff} endpoints that recompute variance server-side (NOT OR /transition); cashShift/cashDiff have no x-openregister-lifecycle; (2) the variance panel stays in the section because it is a LATEST/PENDING-child projection — relatedCollections lists ALL children and cannot pick + lay out the single most-relevant cashDiff with its tolerance verdict and inline approve/reject. Missing primitives: a host-app-endpoint action toolbar (see PosTransactionDetail); a 'latest/pending child object' projection primitive.
pages.title: Shift

config._note: FINANCIAL archetype (bespoke-detail-pages). A cash-drawer shift is a cash-management ledger record, so NO comms leaves (cashShift declares no email/calendar linkedType). The body opens with the opening-float KPI stat then the shift fields (reference, drawer, operator, managedBy, currency, floatAt, status, closedAt, reconciliationStatus) 8-wide and the related graph (drawer, operator) 4-wide. The cash drops stay in the PRESERVED relatedCollections table (cashDrop, FK 'shift') and the cash-reconciliation VARIANCE panel + drop/count/reconcile actions stay in the PRESERVED CashShiftActionsSection bodyWidget (after-related) — the variance panel is a latest/pending-child projection a plain object-list cannot lay out, as its note records. Audit-trail moves to a sidebar tab.

pages._note: Daily Z-report (end-of-day close) ledger as a declarative type:index page (pipelinq-views-to-declarative-r1). pages.title: Boekhoudkundige Afhandeling

pages._note: Z-report per-day close as a declarative type:detail page (pipelinq-detail-pages-declarative-r3). The Z-report's flat fields (reference / reportDate / terminalId / transactionCount / status / subtotal / totalTax / total / bookkeepingStatus / shillinqJournalEntryId / notes) auto-render in the body via CnObjectDataWidget. CONVERTED: the BTW breakdown table, the payment-method breakdown table (both ARRAY fields on the object, not FK children, so not relatedCollections) and the shillinq bookkeeping-status projection + manager-gated idempotent re-raise action are one kind:'section' bodyWidget (ZReportBookkeepingSection, after-data). KEPT-AS-NOTE: (1) lifecycleActions is NOT wired — posZReport has no x-openregister-lifecycle and the only state-changing action is the re-raise, which POSTs to a bespoke pipelinq endpoint (idempotency key) not OR's /transition, so it stays inside the section (missing primitive: declarative action that POSTs to a host-app endpoint instead of OR /transition); (2) no summaryAggregates — the totals are fields ON the object, not aggregations over a related schema; (3) Z-reports are generated by the day-close job, never created/edited by hand, so the auto-body data widget is effectively read-only.
pages.title: Z-report

config._note: FINANCIAL archetype (bespoke-detail-pages). A Z-report is the end-of-day close ledger record, generated by the day-close job and read-only by hand — so NO comms leaves (posZReport declares no email/calendar linkedType) and no object-list (the day's transactions are referenced by the transactionIds ARRAY on the object, not a FK child schema, so there is no single-schema collection to list). The body opens with three KPI stat cards (Day total / VAT / Transaction count) — the headline numbers an accountant checks first — then the report fields (reference, reportDate, terminalId, status, subtotal/discount/total, bookkeepingStatus, shillinqJournalEntryId) full-width. The BTW + payment-method breakdown tables (also arrays-on-object) and the shillinq re-raise action stay in the PRESERVED ZReportBookkeepingSection bodyWidget (after-data), as its note records. Audit-trail moves to a sidebar tab.

pages._note: POS transaction record as a declarative type:detail page (pipelinq-pos-mdm-detail-declarative). The transaction's flat fields (reference / cashier / terminalId / status / priceMode / subtotal / totalTax / total / notes / …) auto-render in the body via CnObjectDataWidget; the line items render as a relatedCollections table (posTransactionLine, FK 'transaction'). Everything no declarative primitive can express lives in one kind:'section' bodyWidget (PosTransactionActionsSection, after-related): the status-gated action toolbar (Bevestigen / Parkeren / Hervatten / Afrekenen / Retour registreren / Terugboeken / Print / Email Receipt), the tax-breakdown + totals, the interactive TenderEntryPanel (live add/remove split tenders + recompute) and the PaymentStatusCard. KEPT-AS-NOTE: lifecycleActions is NOT wired — the action buttons POST to bespoke /api/pos-transactions/{id}/{action} endpoints with side-effects (NOT OR's /transition), and posTransaction has no x-openregister-lifecycle. Missing primitive: a declarative action-toolbar whose buttons POST to a host-app endpoint (not OR /transition), status-gated client-side, with a custom-recompute reload; and an editable/interactive sub-grid primitive for the tender panel.
pages.title: Transactie

config._note: FINANCIAL archetype (bespoke-detail-pages). A POS transaction is a receipt/ledger record — so deliberately NO comms leaves (posTransaction declares no email/calendar linkedType; the receipt is a financial artefact, not a conversation). The body opens with three KPI stat cards (Total / Tax / Line count) so a cashier or auditor reads the money first, then the transaction fields (reference, cashier, terminal, tender, status, priceMode, subtotal/discount/total) 8-wide and the related graph (client/customer, paymentProvider) 4-wide. The line-item register stays in relatedCollections (posTransactionLine, FK 'transaction') and the status-gated action toolbar + interactive tender panel stay in the PRESERVED PosTransactionActionsSection bodyWidget (after-related) — both already carry the missing-primitive notes. Audit-trail moves to a sidebar tab, the correct home for the immutable change log of a financial record.

config._note: Config/ops archetype. A queue is a routing-configuration record (categories, capacity, sort order, assigned agents) — not an entity anyone communicates with — so there are deliberately NO comms leaves and NO files. The body leads with the config data widget and the assigned-agents related graph, and a stats-block KPI card (rule 2, replacing the retired summaryAggregate) chipping the live queue depth @objectId-scoped, then a full-width object-list of the requests currently routed to this queue (request, FK 'queue', View-all -> Requests index) — the queue's whole reason to exist is the work waiting in it, so seeing that backlog is the primary task here. Sidebar is audit-only.

content.emptyText: No requests are routed to this queue right now.

pages._note: MyWork.vue is a personal cross-entity worklist: it merges tasks, deals and contactmomenten assigned to the current user into grouped, due-date-coloured sections with entity badges and quick-filter buttons; no single-register 'index' page can aggregate across these schemas.
pages.title: My Work

pages._note: Lead analytics as a declarative type:dashboard page (pipelinq-dashboards-declarative). The surface has no headline KPI cards to lift into endpoint stat widgets — its four bespoke widgets (pipeline-value funnel bar chart, source-performance table, lead-aging donut, win/loss pie + KPI block) are fed from ONE GET /api/rapportage/pipeline-stats fetch and the interactivity lives INSIDE the widgets (the funnel's OR-sourced pipeline selector filters in memory; the win/loss date-range selector re-fetches with dateFrom/dateTo). All four therefore live in one kind:'section' bodyWidget (LeadAnalyticsSection) which preserves the legacy single-fetch + in-widget filtering verbatim. KEPT-AS-NOTE: no page-level period pageFilter — the date window is derived inside the win/loss range selector (a from/to pair a static select cannot emit) and the pipeline selector's options are OR-sourced; missing primitives: derived-date-range pageFilter + OR-collection pageFilter options.
pages.title: Analytics

pages._note: Contact-reporting monitor as a declarative type:dashboard page (pipelinq-dashboards-declarative). The four headline KPIs (Total Contacts, FCR %, Avg Handling Time, SLA Compliance) are endpoint-bound stat widgets reading GET /apps/pipelinq/api/rapportage/kpis (avgHandlingTime is a pre-formatted 'H:MM' string the stat widget renders verbatim). A period pageFilter (today/week/month -> @page.period) drives the query; ReportingController now resolves that relative period to a from/to window server-side (today=[today,today], week=[Monday,today], month=[1st,today]) so one select re-queries every KPI without client-side date math. The hand-rendered per-channel bar chart + the CSV export the stat grid cannot express live in one kind:'section' bodyWidget (ChannelDistributionSection) that reads the same period (via @workspace.period) and self-fetches /api/rapportage/channels. The 60s auto-refresh + 'last updated' label of the legacy view are dropped (the page-level Refresh action covers manual reload).
pages.title: Contact reporting

pages._note: Cross-channel comparison as a declarative type:dashboard page (pipelinq-dashboards-declarative). It has no headline KPI cards — the cross-channel comparison table (total / FCR / SLA per channel, colour-keyed) lives entirely in one kind:'section' bodyWidget (ChannelComparisonSection). Two pageFilters drive it: period (today/week/month -> @page.period, resolved to from/to server-side by ReportingController) and granularity (daily/weekly -> @page.granularity); the section reads both via @workspace.* and self-fetches /api/rapportage/channels + /api/rapportage/sla.
pages.title: Channel analytics

pages._note: Per-agent performance as a declarative type:dashboard page (pipelinq-dashboards-declarative). It has no headline KPI cards — the sortable per-agent leaderboard (contacts / avg time / FCR) plus the team-summary footer (total contacts, team FCR, both derived from the same agents map) live in one kind:'section' bodyWidget (AgentPerformanceSection).
